s1.syndrome_frame: Gradually enlarging, asymptomatic, reddish-brown skin lesion with peripheral ecchymosis
salient_findings: Reddish-brown annular plaque with peripheral ecchymosis
Poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation
key_facts: Previous treatment with topical antifungal cream showed no improvement
Vascular channel endothelial cells positive for CD31, CD34, and D2-40
Negative for human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) and Wilms tumor 1 (WT1)
Ki-67 index showed low proliferation in endothelial cells
HIV, Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C serologic tests negative

shortlist.label: Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of a gradually enlarging, asymptomatic, reddish-brown skin lesion with peripheral ecchymosis and histologic findings of vascular proliferation and hemosiderin deposits

shortlist.label: Hobnail hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Shares similar histologic features, including vascular channels lined with bland endothelial cells and presence of hemosiderin deposits

shortlist.label: Spindle cell hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Presents with similar clinical and histologic characteristics, including a reddish-brown lesion and vascular proliferation

shortlist.label: Glomeruloid hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation and histologic findings, including the presence of vascular channels and hemosiderin deposits

shortlist.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely due to negative HHV-8 testing, it remains a consideration given the clinical presentation of a reddish-brown skin lesion

raw.rationale: The clinical presentation of a gradually enlarging, asymptomatic, reddish hematomalike plaque with a brownish peripheral border, combined with the histologic findings of poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation and the presence of promontory signs, is consistent with targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma. The immunohistochemical profile, including positivity for CD31, CD34, and D2-40, and the absence of HHV-8 and WT1, also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Hobnail hemangioma
rejected.why: While hobnail hemangioma can present with similar clinical features, the histologic findings and immunohistochemical profile in this case are more consistent with targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma.

rejected.label: Spindle cell hemangioma
rejected.why: Spindle cell hemangioma typically presents with a more complex vascular proliferation and a higher degree of cellular atypia, which is not seen in this case.

rejected.label: Glomeruloid hemangioma
rejected.why: Glomeruloid hemangioma is typically associated with POEMS syndrome and has a distinct histologic appearance, which is not consistent with this case.

rejected.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
rejected.why: Kaposi's sarcoma is typically associated with HHV-8 positivity, which is negative in this case, and has a distinct histologic appearance with more pronounced cellular atypia and mitotic activity.
